scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #9013: Routes for the R7 region -- 17.x.x.x (R7 loopbacks), 67.0.0.0/8
(the R6-R7 link), and 70.0.0.0/8 (R7 LAN) -- disappeared from R1's routing table.
R6 is logging that its OSPF neighbor went down. The team is convinced R6's OSPF
process (or its configuration) broke the adjacency. Please confirm the R6 fault
and identify the affected interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath5-r7-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R7. R7 owns
the 17.1.{1..4}.0/24 loopbacks and the 70.0.0.0/8 LAN, and forms the only OSPF
adjacency with R6 over 67.0.0.0/8. With R7's ospfd stopped, R6 ages out R7's LSAs
and the withdrawals propagate through area 1 and the backbone, so R1 loses the
whole R7 region -- exactly the reported pattern.

The TWIST: the ticket blames R6. R6 is HEALTHY -- its ospfd is running and its
OTHER OSPF adjacencies are Full; it is merely reporting that its neighbor R7
disappeared. This is symptom-site bias: the team watches the router that logged
the event. A decisive tell: only the R6<->R7 adjacency dropped while R6's other
adjacencies stayed up -- if R6 were the cause, those would be affected too; the
common failure is R7.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r7 (ospfd not running). The
agent must localise from evidence -- R7's dead ospfd and R7's prefixes withdrawn
domain-wide -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on R6. An agent that "confirms the
R6 OSPF fault" has followed the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix:
`/etc/init.d/frr restart` on R7.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r7" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on r7 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
r7). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets r7.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault lies entirely on r7, not r6. R7's OSPF daemon (ospfd) is not running
and its FRR configuration contains no "router ospf" block whatsoever — the process
was never started or its configuration was lost. R6, by contrast, is healthy: it
holds correct OSPF network statements including "network 67.0.0.0/8 area 1" which
covers its eth2 link (67.1.1.1/8) toward R7, and it has stable Full adjacencies
with R4 and R5. Because R7 emits no OSPF Hello packets, R6 cannot form or maintain
a neighbor relationship with it, which is why R6 logs the adjacency as down — R6 is
the victim, not the cause.

With no OSPF process on R7, none of R7's prefixes are injected into the OSPF domain:
the four loopback addresses (17.1.1.1–17.1.4.1/24), the R6–R7 transit link
(67.0.0.0/8, visible only as R6's own connected network), and the R7 LAN
(70.1.1.1/8) are all absent from R1's routing table, exactly matching the reported
symptom. The 67.0.0.0/8 entry that does appear in R1 is R6's own connected prefix,
not an R7-originated LSA, so R7 itself remains unreachable.

Root cause: ospfd is not running on r7, and r7 has no OSPF configuration.

Corrective fix: On r7, add a "router ospf" block to /etc/frr/frr.conf with
"network 17.0.0.0/8 area 1", "network 67.0.0.0/8 area 1", and "network
70.0.0.0/8 area 1" (matching R6's area 1), enable ospfd in /etc/frr/daemons, and
restart FRR. The R6–R7 adjacency will re-form and all three prefix groups will
propagate to R1.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names the OSPF routing daemon (ospfd) as the failed component on R7 and describes restarting/enabling it as the fix.
Proposes enabling/adding OSPF config on r7, enabling ospfd, and restarting FRR so r7 will form adjacency and re-advertise the missing routes—matching the expected fix.

The investigation log directly shows ospfd is not running on R7, R6 has other Full adjacencies but no R7 neighbor, R7's interfaces and loopbacks exist but are not being advertised; the writeup's inferences about cause and fix follow logically and cover necessary checks. Evidence in the log (show ip ospf neighbor on R7, R6 neighbor table, R7 ip addresses, R1 routes) supports the conclusion that R7's ospfd/config is the fault, not R6.
